questions.text: Select the correct meaning of the idiom "to burn the midnight oil".

options.label: B
options.text: to work late into the night

questions.solution: Shortcut: Recognise the idiom as a fixed expression meaning "to study or work late at night"; discard the literal interpretations (lighting a lamp, wasting time, celebrating). Full solution: The phrase originates from the practice of using oil lamps for light while working after dark. It figuratively means putting in extra effort by staying up late. Option B captures this sense exactly.
Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa in the early 16th century. Vincent van Gogh is known for Starry Night, Pablo Picasso for Guernica, and Michelangelo for the Sistine Chapel ceiling.

questions.text: Choose the word that correctly completes the sentence: 'The _____ of the meeting was postponed due to the storm.'
questions.solution: 'Commencement' means the start or beginning. In this context, the start of the meeting was delayed. While 'venue' (location) and 'agenda' (topics) could be affected by a storm, they are not typically described as being 'postponed' in the same way an event's start time is. 'Conclusion' refers to the end.

questions.text: Deficiency of which vitamin specifically leads to impaired blood clotting and increased bleeding tendency?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Mnemonic **'K** for **K**oagulation' (German spelling). Vitamin K is essential for gamma-carboxylation of clotting factors II, VII, IX, X. Eliminate D (Calcium/Bones), E (Antioxidant/Neuromuscular), A (Vision/Epithelial). Step-by-step: Vitamin K (Phylloquinone/Menaquinone) acts as a cofactor for the enzyme gamma-glutamyl carboxylase, which modifies glutamate residues on clotting factors to bind Calcium ions. Without it, factors remain inactive, causing hemorrhagic disease. Newborns are routinely given Vitamin K prophylaxis.

questions.text: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word: "She has been working here ______ 2015."
questions.solution: Shortcut: "Since" is used with a specific point in time (2015), while "for" is used with a duration. The other options do not fit the present perfect continuous structure. Full solution: The sentence uses present perfect continuous ("has been working") to indicate an action started at a point in the past and continuing. The correct preposition for a starting point is "since". "For" would require a period (e.g., "for eight years"), and "from"/"by" are ungrammatical here.

questions.text: As per the table, which country has the highest per‑capita electricity consumption (kWh) in 2022?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Look for the largest number quickly by scanning the 'kWh per capita' column; the highest value stands out. Full solution: The table shows Norway with 23,500 kWh, India 1,200 kWh, Australia 9,800 kWh, Brazil 2,300 kWh. Hence, Norway has the highest per‑capita consumption.

questions.text: As of February 2024 (after the World Wetlands Day designations), which Indian state has the highest number of Ramsar Sites (Wetlands of International Importance)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Tamil Nadu has been the focus of massive recent additions (14 sites added in July 2022 alone, 2 more in 2023, 5 more on World Wetlands Day Feb 2024). It overtook Uttar Pradesh (traditionally high) to become the clear leader. Current count (Feb 2024): TN ~16, UP ~10. Full Solution: As per the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), India has 80 Ramsar sites as of February 2024. Tamil Nadu leads the tally with 16 designated sites following the addition of five new wetlands (Karaivetti Bird Sanctuary, Longwood Shola Reserve Forest, etc.) on World Wetlands Day (2 Feb 2024). Uttar Pradesh follows with 10 sites. Gujarat has 8 and Punjab has 6. This fact is frequently updated in current affairs for competitive exams.

questions.text: Choose the one‑word substitution for "A person who is indifferent to pleasure or pain".
questions.solution: Shortcut: Eliminate words that denote strong attitudes toward pleasure/pain: "epicurean" and "hedonist" seek pleasure, "ascetic" denies pleasure. The remaining "stoic" means enduring without complaint. Full solution: A stoic is someone who remains calm and indifferent to both pleasure and pain, a core tenet of Stoic philosophy. The other options describe opposite or different attitudes, making "stoic" the correct substitution.

questions.text: Which of the following criteria was assigned the highest weight by the 15th Finance Commission (2021-26) for horizontal devolution of the divisible pool of taxes among States?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The equity principle dominates horizontal devolution; 'Income Distance' (per capita GSDP gap) consistently receives the highest weight (45% in 15th FC) to bridge fiscal disparities. Forest & Ecology (10%) and Demographic Performance (12.5%) are lower. Full Solution: The 15th Finance Commission assigned weights as follows: Income Distance 45%, Population (2011) 15%, Area 15%, Forest & Ecology 10%, Demographic Performance 12.5%, Tax Effort 2.5%. Income Distance ensures poorer states get a larger share.

questions.text: Refer to the table showing Literacy Rates (Census 2011) for four states. Which state has the highest absolute gap between Male and Female literacy rates? | State | Male Literacy (%) | Female Literacy (%) | |---|---|---| | Kerala | 96.1 | 92.1 | | Mizoram | 93.3 | 89.3 | | Goa | 92.6 | 84.7 | | Tripura | 91.5 | 82.7 |
questions.solution: Shortcut: Subtract mentally using 'difference from 90' or unit digits. Kerala: 96.1-92.1 = 4.0. Mizoram: 93.3-89.3 = 4.0. Goa: 92.6-84.7 = 7.9. Tripura: 91.5-82.7 = 8.8. Option elimination: Kerala & Mizoram tied at 4%. Compare Goa (7.9%) vs Tripura (8.8%). Tripura highest. Worked: Calculate gaps: Kerala=4.0%, Mizoram=4.0%, Goa=7.9%, Tripura=8.8%. Tripura has the maximum gap.

questions.text: Match the following Agni missile variants with their correct range classification: 1. Agni-I 2. Agni-III 3. Agni-V Range Classes: (a) Short Range Ballistic Missile (SRBM) (b) Intermediate Range Ballistic Missile (IRBM) (c) Intercontinental Ballistic Missile (ICBM)
questions.solution: Shortcut: Range increases with the missile number (I < II < III < IV < V). Classification thresholds: SRBM < 1,000 km; IRBM 3,000–5,500 km; ICBM > 5,500 km. Agni-I (~700–1,200 km) fits SRBM (Option a). Agni-III (~3,500–5,000 km) fits IRBM (Option b). Agni-V (~5,000–8,000+ km) fits ICBM (Option c). Sequence: 1-a, 2-b, 3-c. Full Solution: The Agni series follows a progressive range enhancement. Agni-I is a single-stage, solid-fuel, road/rail mobile missile with a range of 700–1,200 km, classifying it as an SRBM. Agni-III is a two-stage, solid-fuel IRBM with a range of 3,000–5,000 km. Agni-V is a three-stage, solid-fuel, canisterised ICBM with a proven range exceeding 5,000 km (tested up to 7,000+ km), placing it firmly in the ICBM category. Therefore, the correct matching is 1-a, 2-b, 3-c.

questions.text: The table lists the number of UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage elements for four countries. Which country has exactly double the number of elements as Brazil?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Find Brazil's count, then look for a country with twice that number. Full solution: Brazil has 6 elements. Double is 12. The table shows Japan 8, France 10, South Korea 12, Nigeria 7. South Korea has 12, which is double Brazil's 6.

questions.text: Which of the following was explicitly REJECTED by the Cabinet Mission Plan (1946) during its negotiations with Indian political leaders?

options.label: A
options.text: Grouping of provincial assemblies into Sections A, B, and C

options.label: B
options.text: Formation of a Constituent Assembly elected by Provincial Assemblies

options.label: C
options.text: The demand for a separate sovereign state of Pakistan

options.label: D
options.text: A three-tier federal structure with a weak Centre controlling only Defence, Foreign Affairs, and Communications

questions.solution: Shortcut: The Cabinet Mission (May 1946) was the *last major attempt* to keep India united. Its defining feature was the **rejection of Partition/Pakistan**. The acceptance of Pakistan happened over a year later via the Mountbatten Plan (June 3, 1947). Options A, B, and D were core *recommendations* of the Mission. Full Solution: The Cabinet Mission Plan, announced on 16 May 1946, proposed a united India with a federal structure. It rejected the Muslim League's demand for a separate sovereign Pakistan, arguing that it would not solve the communal problem (large non-Muslim minorities would remain in Pakistan and vice versa) and would entail economic/administrative dislocation. Instead, it proposed: (1) A Union of India controlling Defence, Foreign Affairs, Communications (Option D); (2) Grouping of existing provinces into three Sections (A, B, C) (Option A); (3) A Constituent Assembly elected by Provincial Legislatures to frame the Constitution (Option B). The Mission's rejection of Pakistan is a standard historical fact distinguishing it from the subsequent Mountbatten Plan.

questions.text: The 'Basic Structure' doctrine of the Indian Constitution, which limits Parliament's power to amend the Constitution, was first propounded by the Supreme Court in which landmark case?

options.label: A
options.text: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)

options.label: C
options.text: Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980)

options.label: D
options.text: Shankari Prasad v. Union of India (1951)

questions.solution: Shortcut (Option Elimination): Use chronological logic. Shankari Prasad (1951) and Golaknath (1967) pre-date the doctrine's formulation; they dealt with whether Fundamental Rights are amendable. Minerva Mills (1980) applied the doctrine to strike down parts of the 42nd Amendment. Only Kesavananda Bharati (1973) fits as the originating 13-judge bench verdict. Step-by-step: The doctrine evolved through conflict between Parliament and Judiciary. Early cases (Shankari Prasad, Sajjan Singh) upheld absolute amendment power. Golaknath (1967) reversed this, making FRs unamendable. The 24th Amendment nullified Golaknath. In Kesavananda Bharati (1973), the SC ruled Parliament can amend any article but cannot alter the 'Basic Structure' (supremacy of Constitution, republican/democratic form, secularism, separation of powers, federalism). Minerva Mills (1980) later reinforced this by striking down clauses removing judicial review.

questions.text: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: 'We need to _____ our resources before they run out.'
questions.solution: 'Manage' means to handle or deal with effectively, which fits the context of using time wisely. 'Squander', 'destroy', and 'hide' all imply misuse or loss of time.
